intro: Ler means to read. It's irregular: the present is leio, lês, lê, lemos, leem, and the perfeito eu form is just li. You'll use it for books, news, messages and signs.

presente.pt: Eu [leio] o jornal todas as manhãs.
presente.en: I read the newspaper every morning.
What do you read before going to sleep?

presente.pt: A minha filha já [lê] muito bem.
presente.en: My daughter already reads very well.
We read one book a month.
They read the news on their phones.

perfeito.en: I read that book last summer.

perfeito.pt: Já [leste] a mensagem que te enviei?
perfeito.en: Have you read the message I sent you?

perfeito.pt: [Lemos] o menu e pedimos o peixe.
perfeito.en: We read the menu and ordered the fish.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I used to read comics.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [lia] o jornal ao pequeno-almoço.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to read the paper at breakfast.
We used to read stories before going to sleep.
They were reading while they waited for the train.

futuro.en: I'll read the report tomorrow.
Will you read my book?

futuro.pt: Ela [lerá] o texto em voz alta.
futuro.en: She will read the text aloud.

futuro.pt: Vocês [lerão] o capítulo dois para segunda-feira.
futuro.en: You'll read chapter two for Monday.

condicional.en: I would read more if I had time.
Would you read this book again?

condicional.pt: Nós [leríamos] o jornal, mas não há tempo.
condicional.en: We would read the paper, but there's no time.

condicional.pt: Eles [leriam] tudo em português, se pudessem.
condicional.en: They would read everything in Portuguese if they could.

presente.en: She reads the news on her phone.
presente.pt: Ela lê as notícias no telemóvel.

perfeito.en: I read the whole book in two days.
perfeito.pt: Li o livro todo em dois dias.

imperfeito.en: I used to read a lot as a child.
She was reading when I arrived.
imperfeito.pt: Ela estava a ler quando cheguei.

imperfeito.en: We used to read the paper on Sundays.

futuro.en: I'm going to read it tomorrow.
Are you going to read the email?
They're going to read the text in class.
futuro.pt: Eles vão ler o texto na aula.

condicional.en: I would read more if I had time.
Would you read this?
We would read in Portuguese.

notes.presente: Watch the accents: lês and lê, but lemos. Since the spelling reform, 'they read' is leem (older texts write lêem). For an action in progress, say estou a ler.
notes.perfeito: Li (I read) is tiny but very common. Lemos is the same in the present and the perfeito; context tells you which.
notes.imperfeito: Lia todas as noites = a habit (I used to read). Li o livro ontem = one finished action (I read the book yesterday).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: vou ler, vais ler. With 'it': vou lê-lo (I'm going to read it).

compare.ex: Leio por prazer, mas estudo para o exame.

recap: Leio um pouco todos os dias e já li três livros em português! (I read a little every day and I've already read three books in Portuguese!)

intro: Escrever means to write. It's a regular -er verb in all five tenses (only the past participle, escrito, is irregular). Use it for letters, messages, emails and books.

presente.pt: Eu [escrevo] no meu diário todas as noites.
presente.en: I write in my diary every night.
Do you write with your left hand?
How do you spell your name?

presente.pt: Nós [escrevemos] emails em inglês no trabalho.
presente.en: We write emails in English at work.
The students write a short text.

perfeito.en: I wrote a message to my brother.
Have you written the postcard to Grandma yet?
He wrote a book about Lisbon.
Did you write the right address?

imperfeito.en: In the old days, I used to write letters to my friends.
Did you use to write poems when you were young?
She was writing while I was cooking.
We used to write everything by hand.

futuro.en: I will write the report this week.
He will write the rest of the story.
We will write to the company tomorrow.

futuro.pt: Eles [escreverão] uma carta ao presidente da câmara.
futuro.en: They will write a letter to the mayor.

condicional.pt: Eu [escreveria] um livro, se tivesse tempo.
condicional.en: I would write a book if I had time.

condicional.pt: [Escreverias] uma carta de recomendação para mim?
condicional.en: Would you write a letter of recommendation for me?

condicional.pt: Ela [escreveria] mais depressa com um computador novo.
condicional.en: She would write faster with a new computer.

condicional.pt: Nós [escreveríamos] mais vezes, mas estamos sempre ocupados.
condicional.en: We would write more often, but we're always busy.

presente.en: We write to each other every week.
presente.pt: Escrevemos um ao outro todas as semanas.

imperfeito.en: I used to write letters.
She was writing when the phone rang.
imperfeito.pt: Ela estava a escrever quando o telefone tocou.

imperfeito.en: We used to write everything by hand.

futuro.en: I'm going to write to you tomorrow.
She's going to write a book.
Are you going to write down the address for me?

condicional.en: I would write more, but I'm tired.
Would you write in Portuguese?
We would write a review.

notes.presente: Como se escreve? is the standard way to ask how something is spelled. For an action in progress: estou a escrever.
notes.perfeito: Escrever a alguém = to write to someone. With a pronoun: escrevi-lhe (I wrote to him/her), but não lhe escrevi.
notes.imperfeito: Escrevia cartas = a past habit. Escrevi uma carta = one finished letter.
notes.futuro: In speech you'll mostly hear vou escrever, vou escrever-te (I'm going to write to you).

patterns.en: to write an email / a message

compare.en: to note down / to jot down (also: to point)
compare.ex: Aponta o meu número de telemóvel.

recap: Escrevo um pouco em português todos os dias. (I write a little in Portuguese every day.)

intro: Estudar means to study. It's a regular -ar verb. Use it for school, university, exams and anything you learn on purpose.

presente.en: I've been studying Portuguese for six months.

presente.pt: A minha irmã [estuda] Medicina em Coimbra.
presente.en: My sister studies medicine in Coimbra.
We study together in the library.

presente.pt: Eles [estudam] à noite, depois do trabalho.
presente.en: They study at night, after work.

perfeito.en: I studied a lot for the exam.
Yesterday we studied the irregular verbs.

imperfeito.pt: Quando [estudava] na universidade, vivia com amigos.
imperfeito.en: When I was studying at university, I lived with friends.
She always studied with music on.
We used to study together in secondary school.
They went to the same school.

futuro.en: I will study more next year.
What will you study at university?
We will study chapter five tomorrow.
Will you study in Portugal?

condicional.pt: Eu [estudaria] Direito, se pudesse voltar atrás.
condicional.en: I would study law if I could go back.
Would you study with me tomorrow?
He would study more, but he works a lot.

condicional.pt: Eles [estudariam] no estrangeiro, se tivessem dinheiro.
condicional.en: They would study abroad if they had the money.

presente.pt: Estou a estudar para o teste.

presente.en: We study Portuguese twice a week.
presente.pt: Estudamos português duas vezes por semana.

imperfeito.en: When I was at school, I used to study in the kitchen.
imperfeito.pt: Quando andava na escola, estudava na cozinha.

imperfeito.en: She was studying when I called.
imperfeito.pt: Ela estava a estudar quando liguei.

imperfeito.en: They used to study in the library.

futuro.en: I'm going to study tonight.
She's going to study in Porto.
Are you going to study with me?

condicional.en: I would study more if I had time.
Would you study abroad?
We would study together.

notes.presente: Estudas ou trabalhas? is a classic small-talk question. In Portugal, andar na escola / na universidade also means to be at school / at university.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: estudámos (we studied) vs. estudamos (we study). Brazil writes both as estudamos.
notes.imperfeito: Estudava em Lisboa = I was a student in Lisbon (background). Estudei em Lisboa = I studied in Lisbon (a completed period).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou estudar, vamos estudar.

patterns.en: to study at home / in the library

compare.ex: Estudo muito, por isso aprendo depressa.

recap: Estudo um bocadinho todos os dias e aprendo cada vez mais. (I study a little every day and I learn more and more.)

intro: Perceber means to understand. It's a regular -er verb and, in Portugal, the everyday word for 'to understand', more common in speech than compreender.

presente.en: Do you understand what he's saying?
She knows a lot about computers.

perfeito.en: He understood the problem straight away.
Only later did we realise the mistake.

imperfeito.en: At the beginning, I didn't understand anything.
Did you understand the maths lessons?

imperfeito.pt: Nós não [percebíamos] o sotaque do Porto.
imperfeito.en: We didn't understand the Porto accent.
They understood everything, but they didn't speak.

futuro.en: One day, I'll understand everything.
With time, you'll understand the accent.
He'll understand when he's older.

futuro.pt: Vocês [perceberão] a ideia com este exemplo.
futuro.en: You'll understand the idea with this example.

condicional.en: I would understand better with an example.
Would you understand the film without subtitles?
We would understand more if they spoke slowly.
They wouldn't get the joke.

presente.en: He knows a lot about cars.

perfeito.en: Did you understand what she said?

imperfeito.en: At first I didn't understand anything.
She understood English well.
We didn't understand why.

futuro.en: You'll understand later.
They're going to understand.
I'll understand with time.

condicional.en: I would understand better with an example.
Would you understand without subtitles?
She wouldn't understand.

notes.presente: Perceber is the everyday PT-PT word; Brazilians mostly say entender. Perceber de algo = to know about something: Percebes de vinhos?
notes.perfeito: Percebi! = Got it! Percebemos is the same in the present and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Não percebia nada = a state that lasted (I wasn't understanding anything). Não percebi = I didn't get it (that one time).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vais perceber (you'll understand), vou perceber.

compare.en: to understand / to comprehend (a bit more formal)
to understand (more Brazilian, also used in Portugal)

recap: No início não percebia nada, mas agora percebo quase tudo! (At first I didn't understand anything, but now I understand almost everything!)

intro: Aprender means to learn. It's a regular -er verb. Use aprender a + infinitive for learning to do something: aprender a nadar.

quick.en: It's never too late to learn.

presente.pt: Eu [aprendo] cinco palavras novas por dia.
presente.en: I learn five new words a day.

presente.pt: O meu filho [aprende] tudo com os amigos.
presente.en: My son learns everything from his friends.
We learn a lot from our mistakes.

perfeito.en: I learned to drive at eighteen.

perfeito.pt: Ela [aprendeu] a cozinhar com a avó.
perfeito.en: She learned to cook from her grandmother.

imperfeito.en: At school, I used to learn French.
He used to learn everything by heart.
We used to learn Portuguese songs in class.
They were learning to play the guitar together.

futuro.en: One day I'll learn to play the piano.
With practice, you'll learn quickly.
Tomorrow we'll learn the numbers.
The students will learn to write letters.

condicional.en: I would learn Japanese if I had time.
Would you learn to dance with me?

condicional.pt: Ele [aprenderia] mais com um bom professor.
condicional.en: He would learn more with a good teacher.

condicional.pt: Nós [aprenderíamos] mais depressa a viver em Portugal.
condicional.en: We would learn faster living in Portugal.

presente.en: We learn a lot in class.

perfeito.en: I learned to swim as a child.

imperfeito.en: At school, I used to learn German.
We were learning a lot.
He used to learn everything by heart.

futuro.en: I'm going to learn to drive.
You'll learn with time.
We're going to learn the verbs.

condicional.en: I would learn to cook.
Would you learn Chinese?
They would learn faster in Portugal.
condicional.pt: Eles aprenderiam mais depressa em Portugal.

notes.presente: Aprender a + infinitive: aprendo a nadar (I'm learning to swim). For something in progress, Portuguese uses estou a aprender.
notes.perfeito: Aprendi a conduzir = I learned to drive (and now I can). In Portugal, to drive is conduzir (Brazil: dirigir).
notes.imperfeito: Aprendia francês na escola = background / habit. Aprendi francês em dois anos = a completed result.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou aprender, vais aprender.

compare.ex: O professor ensina e os alunos aprendem.
Estudo todos os dias para aprender mais.

recap: Nunca é tarde para aprender! (It's never too late to learn!)

intro: Ensinar means to teach. It's a regular -ar verb. You ensinar something a alguém (to someone), and ensinar alguém a fazer algo (teach someone to do something).

quick.en: Teach me how to say this.

presente.en: I teach maths at a school.
Will you teach me to make bacalhau?
They teach the children to read.

perfeito.pt: [Ensinei] o meu filho a andar de bicicleta.
perfeito.en: I taught my son to ride a bike.
You taught me everything I know.

perfeito.pt: [Ensinámos] os alunos a usar o computador.
perfeito.en: We taught the students to use the computer.

imperfeito.en: Before, I used to teach at a school in Faro.
My grandfather used to teach me to fish.
We used to teach English in the evenings.
The teachers taught with a lot of patience.

futuro.pt: [Ensinarei] o meu filho a nadar no verão.
futuro.en: I'll teach my son to swim in the summer.
Will you teach at the university?
She will teach French next year.
We'll teach the rules to the new players.

condicional.pt: Eu [ensinaria] português, se tivesse mais experiência.
condicional.en: I would teach Portuguese if I had more experience.
Would you teach small children?
He would teach better with fewer students.
They would teach, but they don't have time.

presente.en: My father teaches me to cook.
presente.pt: O meu pai ensina-me a cozinhar.

imperfeito.en: She used to teach at a school in Lisbon.
imperfeito.pt: Ela ensinava numa escola em Lisboa.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to teach me songs.
We used to teach on Saturdays.

futuro.en: I'm going to teach you a trick.
She's going to teach English in Japan.
futuro.pt: Ela vai ensinar inglês no Japão.

futuro.en: Are you going to teach me tomorrow?

condicional.en: I would teach, but I don't have the patience.
Would you teach children?
They would teach for free.

notes.presente: Two patterns: ensinar alguém a fazer algo (ensino-te a nadar) and ensinar algo a alguém (ensino português a estrangeiros).
notes.perfeito: Quem te ensinou? After quem, the pronoun goes before the verb. Ensinámos (EP) = we taught.
notes.imperfeito: Ensinava em Faro = I used to teach there (background). Ensinei em Faro dois anos = a completed period.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou ensinar-te (I'm going to teach you).

patterns.en: to teach someone to do something

recap: Quem ensina também aprende. (Whoever teaches also learns.)

intro: Explicar means to explain. It's a regular -ar verb; just note the spelling of the perfeito eu form: expliquei (c becomes qu before e to keep the hard sound).

quick.en: I've already explained it to you!
I don't know how to explain.

presente.en: Will you explain to me how it works?

presente.pt: Nós [explicamos] as regras aos novos colegas.
presente.en: We explain the rules to new colleagues.

perfeito.en: I've already explained it to you twice!
Did you explain the problem to the boss?

perfeito.pt: Ela [explicou]-me o caminho para a estação.
perfeito.en: She explained the way to the station to me.
We explained everything to the police.

imperfeito.en: I always used to explain things with drawings.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [explicava]-me os trabalhos de casa.
imperfeito.en: My father used to explain my homework to me.
We were explaining, but nobody was listening.
They used to explain everything very patiently.

futuro.en: I will explain everything at the meeting.
Will you explain to your parents?

futuro.pt: O guia [explicará] a história do castelo.
futuro.en: The guide will explain the history of the castle.
You will explain the project tomorrow.

condicional.en: I would explain, but it's complicated.
Would you explain this in a different way?
That would explain the delay.
We would explain better with an example.

presente.en: Can you explain this to me?
I don't know how to explain.

imperfeito.en: My teacher used to explain everything twice.
imperfeito.pt: A minha professora explicava tudo duas vezes.

imperfeito.en: I was explaining when he left.
imperfeito.pt: Estava a explicar quando ele saiu.

imperfeito.en: They used to explain with examples.

futuro.en: I'll explain later.
She's going to explain the rules.
We're going to explain everything.

condicional.en: That would explain everything.
Would you explain it again?
I would explain, but there's no time.

notes.presente: Explicar algo a alguém. With a pronoun: explica-me (explain to me), but não me explicas (after não).
notes.perfeito: Spelling: expliquei keeps the hard c sound. Explicámos (EP, we explained) vs. explicamos (we explain).
notes.futuro: Colloquially, the present often stands in for the future: Depois explico (I'll explain later). Otherwise: vou explicar.

recap: Não percebeste? Eu explico outra vez! (Didn't you get it? I'll explain again!)

intro: Descobrir means to discover or to find out. It's almost regular, but the stem vowel changes in the eu form of the present: descubro. Everything else follows the -ir pattern (the past participle is descoberto).

presente.pt: Todos os dias [descubro] uma palavra nova.
presente.en: Every day I discover a new word.
You always find the best restaurants.

presente.pt: A minha mãe [descobre] sempre a verdade.
presente.en: My mother always finds out the truth.

presente.pt: Nós [descobrimos] praias novas todos os verões.
presente.en: We discover new beaches every summer.

perfeito.pt: [Descobri] um café muito giro perto de casa.
perfeito.en: I discovered a really nice café near home.
How did you find out my number?
We found out that the museum was closed.

imperfeito.en: On every trip, I used to discover new things.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [descobria] sempre os erros nos textos.
imperfeito.en: He always used to find the mistakes in the texts.
We used to explore the city by bike.

imperfeito.pt: As crianças [descobriam] o mundo a brincar.
imperfeito.en: The children were discovering the world through play.

futuro.en: One day I will find out the truth.
Later you'll find out the answer.
On holiday, we'll discover the Alentejo.
Scientists will discover a cure.

condicional.pt: Eu [descobriria] mais sítios, se tivesse carro.
condicional.en: I would discover more places if I had a car.
How would you find out the answer?
He would find everything out in a minute.
We would never discover this place on our own.

presente.en: Every day I find out something new.
presente.pt: Todos os dias descubro algo novo.

presente.en: Children discover the world through play.
presente.pt: As crianças descobrem o mundo a brincar.

imperfeito.en: On every trip, we used to discover new places.
imperfeito.pt: Em cada viagem, descobríamos sítios novos.

imperfeito.en: She always found the mistakes.
I was discovering the city.

futuro.en: You'll find out tomorrow.
We're going to discover the north.
They're going to find out the truth.

condicional.en: I would never find out.
How would you find out?
She would find the problem quickly.

notes.presente: Only the eu form changes: descubro. Tu descobres, ele descobre and eles descobrem keep the o (pronounced open).
notes.perfeito: Descobri que... = I found out that... Descobrimos is the same in the present and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Descobria = I used to discover / was discovering. Descobri = I found out (at one moment).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vais descobrir, vamos descobrir.

compare.en: to find (something you were looking for) / to meet
to know (soube = I found out / I heard)

recap: Descubro sempre algo novo quando viajo por Portugal. (I always discover something new when I travel around Portugal.)

intro: Desenvolver means to develop. It's a regular -er verb. Use it for projects, skills and products; the reflexive desenvolver-se means to develop or grow by itself.

quick.en: I want to develop my Portuguese.
The city has developed a lot.

presente.pt: Eu [desenvolvo] software para uma empresa no Porto.
presente.en: I develop software for a company in Porto.
How do you develop your ideas?
This company develops products for children.
We develop the project as a team.

presente.pt: As crianças [desenvolvem] a linguagem muito depressa.

perfeito.en: I developed an app for learning languages.

perfeito.pt: A cidade [desenvolveu]-se muito nos últimos anos.
perfeito.en: The city has developed a lot in recent years.

imperfeito.en: At the time, I was developing websites for restaurants.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [desenvolvia] os produtos e ela vendia-os.
imperfeito.en: He developed the products and she sold them.
We used to develop everything at home.
They used to develop mobile games.

futuro.en: I will develop the project next year.
The company will develop an electric car.
We will develop the idea together.
The students will develop their skills.

condicional.pt: Eu [desenvolveria] esta ideia, se tivesse dinheiro.
condicional.en: I would develop this idea if I had money.
How would you develop the plan?
That would develop the local economy.
We would develop a new version.

presente.pt: Estamos a desenvolver um produto novo.

presente.en: I want to develop my Portuguese.

imperfeito.en: I used to develop websites.
They were developing a game.
imperfeito.pt: Eles estavam a desenvolver um jogo.

imperfeito.en: The company was growing fast.

futuro.en: We're going to develop the idea.
She's going to develop a new course.
futuro.pt: Ela vai desenvolver um curso novo.

futuro.en: The project is going to develop over time.
futuro.pt: O projeto vai desenvolver-se com o tempo.

condicional.en: I would develop the project differently.
condicional.pt: Desenvolveria o projeto de outra maneira.

condicional.en: Would you develop this idea?
That would develop the region.

notes.presente: Desenvolver (+ object) = to develop something. Desenvolver-se = to develop / grow by itself: A cidade desenvolve-se.
notes.perfeito: Desenvolvemos is the same in the present and the perfeito; context tells you which.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vamos desenvolver, vai desenvolver-se.

recap: Estamos a desenvolver um projeto novo e estou muito entusiasmado! (We're developing a new project and I'm very excited!)

intro: Produzir means to produce. It's regular except for one form: the ele/ela present is produz, with no final -e (like conduzir and traduzir). Use it for farms, factories, films, music and energy.

quick.en: Portugal produces a lot of wine.

presente.en: I produce videos for the internet.
Do you produce your own music?

presente.pt: O Douro [produz] o vinho do Porto.

presente.en: We produce olive oil on our farm.

perfeito.en: I produced my first album in 2020.
This year we produced less wine.
The solar panels produced a lot of energy.

imperfeito.en: In the past, I used to make cheese at home.

imperfeito.pt: A fábrica [produzia] mil carros por dia.
imperfeito.en: The factory used to produce a thousand cars a day.
We used to produce everything we ate.

imperfeito.pt: Os meus avós [produziam] o próprio vinho.
imperfeito.en: My grandparents used to make their own wine.

futuro.en: I will produce a documentary about the Alentejo.
The new factory will produce bicycles.
We will produce more next year.

futuro.pt: Eles [produzirão] uma série para a televisão.
futuro.en: They will produce a TV series.

condicional.en: I would produce more with better machines.
Would you produce a film in Portuguese?
We would produce energy from the wind.

condicional.pt: Estas árvores [produziriam] mais fruta com água.
condicional.en: These trees would produce more fruit with water.

presente.en: Portugal produces a lot of cork.

perfeito.en: The farm produced a lot this year.
perfeito.pt: A quinta produziu muito este ano.

imperfeito.en: My grandparents used to make their own wine.
imperfeito.pt: Os meus avós produziam o próprio vinho.

imperfeito.en: The region used to produce a lot of wheat.
We were producing too much.

futuro.en: They're going to produce a new series.
futuro.pt: Eles vão produzir uma série nova.

futuro.en: We're going to produce less plastic.
This is going to produce good results.

condicional.en: This would produce more energy.
Would you produce your own music?
We would produce more with more people.

notes.presente: Ele produz, not produze. The same happens in conduzir (conduz), traduzir (traduz) and reduzir (reduz), and in fazer and dizer (faz, diz).
notes.perfeito: Produzimos is the same in the present and the perfeito.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vão produzir, vamos produzir.

patterns.en: to produce a film / an album

compare.ex: Faço pão em casa, mas a padaria produz centenas por dia.

recap: Portugal produz vinho, azeite e cortiça de grande qualidade. (Portugal produces top-quality wine, olive oil and cork.)

intro: Parar means to stop. It's a regular -ar verb. Use parar de + infinitive to stop doing something: parar de fumar. Since the spelling reform, ele para has no accent (older texts write pára).

presente.pt: Eu [paro] sempre neste café para beber uma bica.
presente.en: I always stop at this café for an espresso.

presente.pt: O autocarro [para] em frente à escola.
presente.en: The bus stops in front of the school.
We stop for lunch at midday.

perfeito.en: I stopped smoking two years ago.

perfeito.pt: O comboio [parou] no meio do caminho.

perfeito.en: We stopped in Coimbra to eat.

imperfeito.en: Before, I always used to stop at this pastry shop.
She couldn't stop laughing.
We used to stop at every beach.

imperfeito.pt: Os carros [paravam] para deixar passar as pessoas.
imperfeito.en: The cars used to stop to let people cross.

futuro.en: I won't stop until I finish.

futuro.pt: O comboio [parará] em todas as estações.
futuro.en: The train will stop at every station.
We will stop in Porto for two days.
The roadworks will stop in August.

condicional.pt: Eu [pararia] aqui, mas não há lugar.
condicional.en: I would stop here, but there's no space.

condicional.pt: [Pararias] de trabalhar, se ganhasses a lotaria?
condicional.en: Would you stop working if you won the lottery?
He would never stop studying.

condicional.pt: Nós [pararíamos] mais vezes, mas estamos com pressa.
condicional.en: We would stop more often, but we're in a hurry.

presente.en: Does this bus stop at the station?

imperfeito.en: She couldn't stop crying.
We used to stop in every village.
It was raining non-stop.

futuro.en: I'm going to stop here.
When is it going to stop raining?
futuro.pt: Quando é que vai parar de chover?

futuro.en: We're going to stop for lunch.

condicional.en: I would stop, but I'm late.
Would you stop working?
They would never stop talking.

notes.presente: Parar de + infinitivo = to stop doing something: Não para de chover. Since the reform, para (stops) looks like the preposition para; context makes it clear.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: parámos (we stopped) vs. paramos (we stop).
notes.imperfeito: Não parava de... = kept on... : Ela não parava de rir (She couldn't stop laughing).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou parar, vamos parar para almoçar.

patterns.en: to stop (in order) to do something

recap: Não paro de aprender, mesmo quando estou cansado! (I never stop learning, even when I'm tired!)

intro: Continuar means to continue or to carry on. It's a regular -ar verb. In Portugal, continuar a + infinitive means 'to keep doing something' (Brazil uses the gerund instead).

presente.en: Are you still working at the bank?

perfeito.en: Did you keep studying after your degree?

perfeito.pt: Ela [continuou] a falar como se nada fosse.
perfeito.en: She carried on talking as if nothing had happened.
After lunch, we continued our journey.

imperfeito.en: I kept thinking about the exam.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [continuava] a ligar-me todos os dias.
imperfeito.en: He kept calling me every day.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [continuávamos] a caminhar, apesar da chuva.
imperfeito.en: We kept walking, despite the rain.
They still didn't understand anything.

futuro.en: I will keep studying Portuguese.
Will you stay in the same job?

futuro.pt: O tempo quente [continuará] durante a semana.
futuro.en: The hot weather will continue during the week.
We will continue the meeting tomorrow.

condicional.en: I would stay on here if I could.

condicional.pt: Tu [continuarias] a trabalhar depois dos setenta?
condicional.en: Would you keep working after seventy?
He would keep playing, but he got hurt.

condicional.pt: Eles [continuariam] a viagem, mas o carro avariou.
condicional.en: They would continue the trip, but the car broke down.

perfeito.en: We continued the journey by train.

imperfeito.en: He kept calling me.
They kept on working.
I was still thinking about it.

futuro.en: We'll carry on tomorrow.
Are you going to keep studying?
Prices are going to keep rising.
futuro.pt: Os preços vão continuar a subir.

condicional.en: I would carry on, but I'm tired.
Would you keep working here?
We would continue the project.

notes.presente: PT-PT: continuar a + infinitivo (continuo a estudar). Brazil: continuar + gerund (continuo estudando). Continuo a viver aqui also means 'I still live here'.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: continuámos (we continued) vs. continuamos (we continue).
notes.imperfeito: Continuava a... describes something that kept going on in the past: Ele continuava a ligar-me.
notes.futuro: The present often expresses a near future: Continuamos amanhã (We'll carry on tomorrow). Otherwise: vou continuar a...

compare.ex: Fico em casa, mas continuo a trabalhar.

recap: Continuo a estudar português todos os dias! (I keep studying Portuguese every day!)

intro: Precisar means to need. It's a regular -ar verb, but remember that it takes de: preciso de ajuda, preciso de sair. In Portugal the de is kept even before an infinitive.

presente.en: Do you need help with the suitcases?

perfeito.pt: [Precisei] de um médico ontem à noite.
perfeito.en: I needed a doctor last night.

perfeito.pt: Ele [precisou] de ajuda para mudar de casa.
perfeito.en: He needed help to move house.

perfeito.pt: [Precisámos] de um táxi para chegar a horas.
perfeito.en: We needed a taxi to arrive on time.

imperfeito.en: I needed to speak to you.
She needed to rest.
We needed more time.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [precisavam] de dinheiro para a viagem.
imperfeito.en: They needed money for the trip.

futuro.en: I will need the car on Saturday.
You'll need a coat in Bragança.
The project will need more people.
You'll need your passports.

condicional.en: I would need one more week.

condicional.pt: [Precisarias] de visto para ir ao Brasil?
condicional.en: Would you need a visa to go to Brazil?
We would need a bigger house.
They would need a translator.

imperfeito.en: I needed to talk to you.
She needed a holiday.
They needed money.

futuro.en: You're going to need a coat.
We're going to need help.
Are you going to need the car tomorrow?

condicional.en: I would need more time.
Would you need help?
They would need a bigger house.
condicional.pt: Eles precisariam de uma casa maior.

notes.presente: In PT-PT it's always precisar de: preciso de comer (Brazil often drops the de before an infinitive). De + o = do: preciso do carro.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: precisámos (we needed) vs. precisamos (we need).
notes.imperfeito: Precisava de... is also a polite way to ask for something: Precisava de uma informação (I'd need some information).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vais precisar de um casaco (you're going to need a coat).

compare.ex: Tenho de sair, preciso de apanhar o comboio.

recap: Se precisares de alguma coisa, liga-me! (If you need anything, call me!)

intro: Aumentar means to increase, to raise or to go up. It's a regular -ar verb. Use it for prices, salaries, volume, temperature and numbers.

quick.en: The temperature is going to rise.

presente.pt: Eu [aumento] o volume quando gosto da música.
presente.en: I turn up the volume when I like the music.
Can you turn up the heating? I'm cold.

presente.pt: O trânsito [aumenta] às seis da tarde.
presente.en: Traffic increases at six in the evening.
We raise our prices in January.

perfeito.pt: [Aumentei] o número de aulas por semana.
perfeito.en: I increased the number of lessons per week.
Did you turn up the oven temperature?
My boss gave me a pay rise.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [aumentava] sempre o volume do rádio.
imperfeito.en: I always used to turn up the radio.
The noise kept getting louder.
We used to speed up on the straights.
Prices were going up every month.

futuro.en: I will increase my study time.

futuro.pt: O preço da gasolina [aumentará] em março.
futuro.en: The price of petrol will go up in March.
We will raise salaries next year.

futuro.pt: As temperaturas [aumentarão] no fim de semana.
futuro.en: Temperatures will rise at the weekend.

condicional.en: I would raise the minimum wage.
Would you turn up the volume, please?
That would increase the risk.
They would raise the rent if they could.

presente.pt: As rendas aumentam todos os anos.

perfeito.en: My boss gave me a raise.
perfeito.pt: O meu chefe aumentou-me o salário.

imperfeito.en: The noise kept getting louder.
imperfeito.pt: O barulho aumentava cada vez mais.

imperfeito.en: Prices were going up every month.
imperfeito.pt: Os preços aumentavam todos os meses.

imperfeito.en: The pain was getting worse.

futuro.en: Prices are going to go up.
The temperature is going to rise.
We're going to increase production.

condicional.en: That would increase the risk.
Would you raise the price?
I would raise the minimum wage.

notes.presente: Aumentar works both ways: aumento o volume (I turn it up) and o volume aumenta (it goes up). The opposite is diminuir.
notes.perfeito: Aumentou-me o salário = gave me a raise. The noun is um aumento (a raise / an increase). EP spelling: aumentámos.
notes.imperfeito: Aumentava cada vez mais = kept increasing (a gradual process in the past).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: os preços vão aumentar.

patterns.en: to raise the price / the salary

recap: Os preços aumentam, mas o meu salário não! (Prices go up, but my salary doesn't!)

intro: Diminuir means to decrease, to reduce or to turn down. It's an -uir verb, so the endings shift slightly: tu diminuis, ele diminui (not -ues, -ue), and an accent appears on the stressed í (diminuímos, diminuí, diminuía). Incluir and contribuir work the same way.

presente.en: I'm cutting down the sugar in my coffee.
Can you turn the volume down, please?
The pain eases with this medicine.
We're reducing how much meat we eat.
The days get shorter in winter.

perfeito.en: I slowed down near the school.
Did you cut down your working hours?

imperfeito.pt: Eu [diminuía] o volume quando o bebé dormia.
imperfeito.en: I used to turn the volume down when the baby was sleeping.
The noise used to die down at night.
We used to turn the heating down to save money.
Sales were dropping every month.

futuro.en: I will cut down my time on the phone.
The price will go down next month.
We will reduce plastic in the office.

futuro.pt: As temperaturas [diminuirão] no fim de semana.
futuro.en: Temperatures will drop at the weekend.

condicional.en: I would lower taxes.
Would you turn the volume down, please?
That would reduce traffic in the city.

condicional.pt: Eles [diminuiriam] o preço, se comprássemos dois.
condicional.en: They would lower the price if we bought two.

presente.en: The days get shorter in winter.

imperfeito.en: The noise was dying down.
Sales were going down every month.
imperfeito.pt: As vendas diminuíam todos os meses.

imperfeito.en: We used to turn the heating down at night.

futuro.en: Prices are going to drop.
I'm going to cut down on sugar.
The pain is going to ease.

condicional.en: That would reduce traffic.
Would you lower the price?
I would cut taxes.

notes.presente: -uir verbs: tu diminuis, ele diminui (no -e), nós diminuímos (with accent). Incluir (incluis, inclui) and contribuir follow the same pattern.
notes.perfeito: Diminuí (I reduced) has an accent; diminui without one is the present (he reduces) or the tu command (turn it down!).
notes.imperfeito: The accent stays in every form: diminuía, diminuías, diminuíamos, diminuíam.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: os preços vão diminuir.

compare.ex: Os preços aumentam e os salários diminuem.

recap: Diminui a velocidade: há uma escola aqui perto! (Slow down: there's a school nearby!)

intro: Manter means to maintain, to keep or to keep up. It's irregular because it's built on ter: mantenho, manténs, mantém (like tenho, tens, tem), and mantive in the perfeito (like tive).

presente.en: You keep the house very clean.

presente.pt: Ela [mantém] o contacto com os colegas da escola.
presente.en: She keeps in touch with her school friends.

presente.pt: Nós [mantemos] a tradição do bacalhau no Natal.
presente.en: We keep up the tradition of bacalhau at Christmas.
They keep the garden looking lovely.

perfeito.en: I kept calm during the interview.
Did you keep in touch with her?
The restaurant kept the same prices.
We kept the booking for Saturday.

imperfeito.en: I used to keep a diary.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [mantinha] a horta sozinho.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather kept up the vegetable garden on his own.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [mantínhamos] as janelas fechadas por causa do calor.
imperfeito.en: We used to keep the windows closed because of the heat.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [mantinham] a loja aberta até tarde.
imperfeito.en: They used to keep the shop open until late.

futuro.en: I will keep my word.
Will you keep the same schedule?
We'll keep in touch, I promise.

futuro.pt: As lojas [manterão] o horário de verão.
futuro.en: The shops will keep their summer opening hours.

condicional.pt: Eu [manteria] o carro velho, mas gasta muito.
condicional.en: I would keep the old car, but it uses a lot of fuel.
Would you keep the secret?
That would keep the children busy.
We would keep the house if we could.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to keep a vegetable garden.
imperfeito.pt: A minha avó mantinha uma horta.

imperfeito.en: We used to keep the door open.
He kept everything in order.

futuro.en: We're going to keep in touch.
I'm going to keep the booking.
Are you going to keep the car?

condicional.en: Would you keep the secret?
I would keep the old furniture.
We would keep the same plan.

notes.presente: Conjugate it like ter with man- in front: mantenho, manténs, mantém, mantemos, mantêm. Watch the accents: manténs, mantém (he keeps), mantêm (they keep).
notes.perfeito: The perfeito copies ter too: tive → mantive, teve → manteve, tiveram → mantiveram.
notes.imperfeito: Like tinha → mantinha. Mantinha um diário = I used to keep a diary.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vamos manter o contacto (let's keep in touch). EP spelling: contacto.

patterns.en: to keep one's word / a promise

compare.en: to keep / to store / to put away

recap: Mantém a calma e continua a estudar! (Keep calm and keep studying!)

intro: Defender means to defend or to stand up for. It's a regular -er verb. Use it for people, ideas and rights, and in sport (the goalkeeper defende a shot = saves it).

presente.en: I always stand up for my friends.
Why do you always defend your brother?

perfeito.en: I defended my idea at the meeting.
You stood up for me when I needed it.

perfeito.pt: [Defendemos] a nossa proposta até ao fim.
perfeito.en: We defended our proposal to the end.

imperfeito.pt: Na escola, [defendia] sempre os mais pequenos.
imperfeito.en: At school, I always used to stand up for the little ones.
The dog used to guard the house.
We held the same opinion.
The soldiers were defending the castle.

futuro.en: I will defend my thesis in June.
Will you play in goal on Saturday?
The lawyer will defend the client.
We will defend the title next year.

condicional.en: I would defend your idea.
Would you defend a friend, even if he was wrong?
He would never defend that.

condicional.pt: Eles [defenderiam] a cidade até ao fim.
condicional.en: They would defend the city to the end.

presente.en: I always stand up for my friends.
She stands up for her ideas.

imperfeito.en: The dog used to guard the house.
I always used to stand up for my sister.
They held the same idea.

futuro.en: I'm going to defend my idea.
The lawyer is going to defend him.
We're going to defend the title.

condicional.en: I would defend this idea.
Would you defend that position?
Nobody would defend that.

notes.presente: Defender alguém = to stand up for someone; defender-se = to defend oneself. In football, Portugal says guarda-redes (goalkeeper) and baliza (goal); Brazil says goleiro and gol.
notes.perfeito: Defendemos is the same in the present and the perfeito. With a pronoun: defendeu-me, but não me defendeu.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou defender. With 'him': vai defendê-lo.

compare.ex: O protetor solar protege a pele.
Uma equipa ataca e a outra defende.

recap: Defendo sempre os meus amigos, mesmo quando não estão presentes. (I always stand up for my friends, even when they're not there.)

intro: Atacar means to attack. It's a regular -ar verb; the only spelling change is ataquei (c becomes qu before e). Use it for armies, animals, sports teams and criticism, and informally for tackling a task.

quick.en: I was attacked in the street.

presente.pt: No futebol, eu [ataco] pelo lado esquerdo.
presente.en: In football, I attack down the left side.
Why do you always attack my ideas?
We attack more in the second half.

perfeito.en: I tackled the problem first thing in the morning.

perfeito.pt: Porque [atacaste] o teu colega na reunião?
perfeito.en: Why did you attack your colleague in the meeting?
We attacked for the whole game.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [atacava] e o meu irmão defendia.
imperfeito.en: I used to attack and my brother defended.

imperfeito.pt: O cão [atacava] todas as pessoas que passavam.
imperfeito.en: The dog used to attack everyone who walked past.
We used to attack more in the first half.
Pirates used to attack ships.

futuro.en: I'll tackle this job tomorrow.
The army will attack at dawn.
We will attack down the wings.
The newspapers will attack the government.

condicional.pt: Eu [atacaria] mais, se fosse o treinador.
condicional.en: I would attack more if I were the coach.
Would you attack or defend?
That dog would never attack a child.
They would attack, but they were tired.

imperfeito.en: I used to attack and he defended.
Pirates used to attack ships.
The team was attacking a lot.
imperfeito.pt: A equipa estava a atacar muito.

futuro.en: They're going to attack in the second half.
futuro.pt: Eles vão atacar na segunda parte.

futuro.en: I'm going to tackle this job tomorrow.
Is the dog going to attack?

condicional.en: That dog would never attack.
Would you attack or defend?
I would attack more.

notes.presente: Atacar alguém (no preposition). With a pronoun: atacou-me, but o cão não me atacou.
notes.perfeito: Spelling: ataquei keeps the hard c sound. EP: atacámos (we attacked) vs. atacamos (we attack).
notes.imperfeito: Atacava = used to attack / was attacking (background). Atacou = attacked (one event).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vão atacar. Informally, atacar um problema / um trabalho = to tackle it.

compare.ex: Uma equipa ataca e a outra defende.

recap: A equipa ataca, mas o guarda-redes defende tudo! (The team attacks, but the goalkeeper saves everything!)

en: to hit / to knock / to beat
intro: Bater means to hit, to knock or to beat. It's a regular -er verb with lots of everyday uses: bater à porta (to knock on the door), o coração bate (the heart beats), bater os ovos (to beat the eggs), bater com o carro (to crash the car).

presente.pt: Eu [bato] à porta e ninguém responde.
presente.en: I knock on the door and nobody answers.

presente.pt: Tu [bates] os ovos e eu faço o resto.
presente.en: You beat the eggs and I'll do the rest.
His heart is beating very fast.

presente.pt: Nós [batemos] palmas no fim do concerto.
presente.en: We clap at the end of the concert.
The waves crash against the rocks.

perfeito.en: I hit my head on the door.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, [batia] com a bola na parede.
imperfeito.en: When I was little, I used to kick the ball against the wall.
The rain was beating against the window.

imperfeito.pt: No Pão-por-Deus, [batíamos] à porta dos vizinhos.
imperfeito.en: On All Saints' Day, we used to knock on the neighbours' doors.
The bells used to ring at midday.

futuro.en: I'll knock on the door before going in.
The athlete will beat the record.
We'll beat their team on Sunday.
They'll clap at the end.

condicional.pt: Eu [bateria] à porta, mas é muito tarde.
condicional.en: I would knock on the door, but it's very late.
You would beat the record with more training.
He would never hit an animal.

condicional.pt: Nós [bateríamos] qualquer equipa, se jogássemos assim.
condicional.en: We would beat any team if we played like this.

presente.pt: Bate à porta antes de entrares.
O meu coração está a bater depressa.

imperfeito.en: The rain was beating on the window.
My heart was beating fast.
We used to knock on the neighbours' doors.

futuro.en: I'm going to knock on the door.
They're going to beat the record.
We're going to beat them.

condicional.en: I would knock, but it's late.
condicional.pt: Bateria à porta, mas é tarde.

condicional.en: He would never hit an animal.
Would you beat the record?

notes.presente: Bater à porta = to knock (on the door). Bater em alguém = to hit someone. Bater com algo = to bang / bump something: bati com o pé (I stubbed my foot).
notes.perfeito: Bateu com o carro = crashed the car. Batemos is the same in the present and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito sets the scene: A chuva batia na janela (The rain was beating on the window).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou bater à porta. With 'them': vamos batê-los.

patterns.pt: bater com a cabeça / com o carro
patterns.en: to hit one's head / to crash the car

compare.en: to touch / to ring (a bell) / to play (music)
compare.ex: Toquei à campainha, mas ninguém abriu.

recap: Alguém está a bater à porta! (Someone is knocking on the door!)

intro: Acreditar means to believe. It's a regular -ar verb, usually followed by em (to believe in / to believe someone) or que (to believe that).

quick.en: I believe you. / I believe in you.

presente.en: She doesn't believe what she sees.
We believe it's going to go well.

presente.pt: Os meus pais [acreditam] muito em mim.
presente.en: My parents really believe in me.

perfeito.en: At first, I didn't believe the news.
We believed until the last minute.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, [acreditava] no Pai Natal.
imperfeito.en: When I was little, I believed in Father Christmas.
Did you use to believe in witches?

imperfeito.pt: Ele [acreditava] em tudo o que lia.
imperfeito.en: He used to believe everything he read.
We thought it was going to rain.

futuro.en: I won't believe any more excuses.
You'll never believe what happened!
Nobody will believe this story.

futuro.pt: Eles [acreditarão] em ti, tenho a certeza.
futuro.en: They will believe you, I'm sure.

condicional.en: I wouldn't believe that.
Would you believe it if I told you?
Nobody would believe it!
They would never believe something like this.

imperfeito.en: When I was little, I believed in Father Christmas.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, acreditava no Pai Natal.

imperfeito.en: She believed everything.
We thought it was going to rain.

futuro.en: They're not going to believe me.
futuro.pt: Eles não vão acreditar em mim.

futuro.en: You won't believe it!
Nobody is going to believe this.

condicional.en: Nobody would believe it.
Would you believe me?
I wouldn't believe that.

notes.presente: Acreditar em (em + o/a = no/na): acredito em ti, acredito no amor. Acreditar que = to believe that. Não acredito! = I can't believe it!
notes.perfeito: European spelling: acreditámos (we believed) vs. acreditamos (we believe).
notes.imperfeito: Acreditava no Pai Natal = an ongoing belief in the past, perfect for the imperfeito.
notes.futuro: Não vais acreditar! (You won't believe it!) is a very common way to start a story.

recap: Acredita em ti e vais conseguir! (Believe in yourself and you'll make it!)

intro: Duvidar means to doubt. It's a regular -ar verb. Use duvidar de (to doubt someone or something) or duvidar que (to doubt that, followed by the subjunctive).

perfeito.en: For a moment, I doubted myself.

imperfeito.en: At the beginning, I doubted everything.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [duvidava] sempre dos vendedores.
imperfeito.en: My father always used to doubt salespeople.
We doubted it was possible.
They used to doubt the news on the internet.

futuro.en: I will never doubt you again.
After this, you'll doubt everything.
Nobody will doubt the result.
Customers will doubt the quality.

condicional.en: I would be suspicious of that offer.
Would you doubt a friend?
Anyone would have doubts.
We would doubt it too.

imperfeito.en: At first I doubted everything.
She doubted the price.
They doubted the news.

futuro.en: Nobody is going to doubt you.
They're going to doubt it.
I'm never going to doubt you again.
futuro.pt: Nunca mais vou duvidar de ti.

condicional.en: I would doubt that offer.
Would you doubt a friend?
Anyone would doubt it.

notes.presente: Duvido! on its own = I doubt it! Duvidar de + noun (de + ele = dele, de + isso = disso). Duvidar que takes the subjunctive: duvido que ele venha.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: duvidámos (we doubted) vs. duvidamos (we doubt).
notes.imperfeito: Duvidava de tudo = a state of doubt in the past. Duvidei por um momento = one moment of doubt.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: ninguém vai duvidar de ti.

recap: Nunca duvides de ti! (Never doubt yourself!)

intro: Ajudar means to help. It's a regular -ar verb and one of the most useful you'll learn. You ajudar alguém (no preposition) and ajudar alguém a + infinitive (help someone to do something).

presente.pt: Eu [ajudo] a minha mãe na cozinha.
presente.en: I help my mother in the kitchen.
Will you help me with the suitcases?

presente.pt: O meu vizinho [ajuda] sempre toda a gente.
Os meus avós [ajudam] a tomar conta das crianças.
presente.en: My grandparents help look after the children.

perfeito.pt: [Ajudei] um turista a encontrar o hotel.
perfeito.en: I helped a tourist find his hotel.
Thanks, you helped me a lot.

perfeito.pt: Ela [ajudou]-me com os trabalhos de casa.
perfeito.en: She helped me with my homework.

perfeito.pt: [Ajudámos] os vizinhos a mudar de casa.
perfeito.en: We helped the neighbours move house.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [ajudava] o meu pai na loja.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to help my father in the shop.

imperfeito.pt: A minha avó [ajudava] toda a gente.
imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to help everyone.
We always used to help at the village festivities.
They used to help each other.

futuro.en: I'll help with whatever is needed.
Will you help organise the party?
This book will help the students.
Will you help clean up afterwards?

condicional.en: I would help, but I don't have time.
Would you help a stranger in the street?
A coffee would help right now!
We would gladly help.

imperfeito.en: I used to help my father.
She always helped everyone.
imperfeito.pt: Ela ajudava sempre toda a gente.

imperfeito.en: They used to help each other.

futuro.en: I'm going to help you.
Are you going to help me tomorrow?
This is going to help.

condicional.en: I would help, but I can't.
A coffee would help.
Would you help a stranger?

notes.presente: Ajudar alguém a fazer algo: ajudo-te a cozinhar. Asking for help: Pode ajudar-me? (formal) / Podes ajudar-me? (informal).
notes.perfeito: The pronoun moves before the verb after não, ninguém, já: ninguém me ajudou. EP spelling: ajudámos. With 'them': ajudámo-los (the s drops).
notes.imperfeito: Ajudava o meu pai = I used to help (habit). Ajudei o meu pai ontem = one occasion.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou ajudar-te (you'll also hear vou-te ajudar in Portugal).

recap: Se precisares, eu ajudo-te! (If you need it, I'll help you!)

intro: Sorrir means to smile. It conjugates like rir, so the present is irregular: sorrio, sorris, sorri, sorrimos, sorriem. Note that sorri can mean 'he smiles', 'I smiled' or 'Smile!'.

presente.pt: Eu [sorrio] sempre que vejo o mar.
presente.en: I smile whenever I see the sea.

presente.pt: Tu [sorris] sempre, mesmo quando estás cansado.
presente.en: You always smile, even when you're tired.

presente.pt: O bebé [sorri] para toda a gente.

perfeito.en: She smiled at me in the street.
We smiled when we heard the news.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [sorria] para todas as câmaras.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to smile at every camera.
My grandfather was always smiling.
We were smiling, but we were nervous.
The tourists were smiling and taking photos.

futuro.en: I'll smile for the photo, I promise.
You'll smile when you see the surprise.
She'll smile when she hears the news.
In the end, we'll all smile.

condicional.en: I would smile more if I slept well.
Would you smile for the camera, please?
He would smile, but he's sad.
They would smile if they understood the joke.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother was always smiling.
imperfeito.pt: A minha avó estava sempre a sorrir.

imperfeito.en: He used to smile a lot.
They were smiling for the photo.

futuro.en: You're going to smile.
Everyone is going to smile.
I'm going to smile for the photo.

condicional.en: Would you smile for the camera?
I would smile, but I'm tired.
She would smile if she saw this.

notes.presente: Sorrir para alguém = to smile at someone (also sorrir a alguém: sorriu-me). Sorri is both 'he smiles' and the tu command 'Smile!'.
notes.perfeito: Sorri (I smiled) and sorrimos (we smiled) look exactly like present forms; context decides.
notes.imperfeito: Sorríamos takes an accent. Estava sempre a sorrir = was always smiling.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vais sorrir, vou sorrir.

patterns.en: to grin from ear to ear

compare.ex: Ela sorriu e depois riu-se muito.

recap: Sorri: estás em Portugal! (Smile: you're in Portugal!)

intro: Rir-se means to laugh. In Portugal it's mostly used reflexively: rio-me, ris-te, ri-se (Brazil usually just says rir). The present is irregular (rio, ris, ri, rimos, riem), and rir-se de means to laugh at.

presente.pt: Eu [rio-me] sempre com os filmes dele.
presente.en: I always laugh at his films.

presente.pt: Os miúdos [riem-se] com os desenhos animados.
presente.en: The kids laugh at the cartoons.

perfeito.en: I laughed so much that I cried.
Did you laugh at my joke?
She laughed when she saw me.
We laughed a lot last night.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to laugh at everything.
The teacher used to laugh with us.
We used to laugh at the same jokes.
They were laughing non-stop.

futuro.en: I promise I won't laugh.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [te rirás] com este filme.
futuro.en: I'm sure you'll laugh at this film.
Nobody will laugh at you.
I know we'll laugh about this one day.

condicional.en: I would laugh too.
Wouldn't you laugh?

condicional.pt: Ninguém [se riria] de uma coisa assim.
condicional.en: Nobody would laugh at something like that.
They would never laugh at you.

presente.pt: Porque é que te estás a rir?

imperfeito.en: We used to laugh at everything.
They were laughing non-stop.
He was laughing at me.
imperfeito.pt: Ele estava a rir-se de mim.

futuro.en: You're going to laugh.
Nobody is going to laugh at you.
futuro.pt: Ninguém se vai rir de ti.

futuro.en: One day we're going to laugh about this.

condicional.en: I would laugh too.
Nobody would laugh.
Wouldn't you laugh?

notes.presente: In PT-PT the reflexive form is the norm: rio-me, ris-te, ri-se, rimo-nos (the s of rimos drops before nos). Rir-se de = to laugh at: Não te rias de mim! Rir-se com = to laugh because of (a film, a joke).
notes.perfeito: Rimo-nos is both 'we laugh' and 'we laughed'. Ri-me = I laughed; ri-se = he laughs.
notes.imperfeito: Ríamo-nos keeps the accent. Ria-me de tudo = I used to laugh at everything.
notes.futuro: The table shows the written form, with the pronoun in the middle (rir-me-ei). It sounds very formal. After não, que, ninguém the pronoun goes in front: não me rirei. In speech just say vou rir-me / vou-me rir.
notes.condicional: Same as the future: the pronoun goes before the verb after words like não, também, nunca: eu também me riria.

patterns.en: to laugh at / because of (a film / a joke)

compare.en: to make fun of / to tease

recap: Rimo-nos tanto que até chorámos! (We laughed so much that we even cried!)

intro: Chorar means to cry. It's a regular -ar verb. Use chorar de (alegria, tristeza) to say why someone cries, and chorar a rir for crying with laughter.

presente.pt: Eu [choro] sempre no fim dos filmes.
presente.en: I always cry at the end of films.

presente.pt: Nós [choramos] a rir com este programa.
presente.en: We cry with laughter at this show.

perfeito.pt: [Chorei] de alegria no casamento da minha irmã.
perfeito.en: I cried with joy at my sister's wedding.
Did you cry at the end of the film?
She cried when she heard the news.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [chorava] no primeiro dia de escola.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to cry on the first day of school.
The baby was crying all night.
We used to cry when the holidays ended.
They were crying because they missed home.

futuro.en: I won't cry over that.
You'll cry with this book.
The baby will cry if he wakes up alone.
The grandparents will cry with joy.

condicional.pt: Eu [choraria], se perdesse o meu cão.
condicional.en: I would cry if I lost my dog.
Would you cry at a film like this?
He would never cry in public.
We would cry with joy.

imperfeito.en: The baby cried all night.
imperfeito.pt: O bebé chorava a noite toda.

imperfeito.en: I used to cry a lot as a child.
She was crying when I arrived.
imperfeito.pt: Ela estava a chorar quando cheguei.

futuro.en: You're going to cry at this film.
I'm not going to cry.
The baby is going to cry.

condicional.en: I would cry.
Would you cry?
He would never cry in public.

notes.presente: For crying right now: está a chorar. Chorar a rir = to cry with laughter.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: chorámos (we cried) vs. choramos (we cry).
notes.imperfeito: O bebé chorava a noite toda describes the background; o bebé chorou quando caiu is one event.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vais chorar, não vou chorar.

recap: Chorei a ver o filme, mas foi um choro bom. (I cried watching the film, but it was a good cry.)

intro: Comer means to eat. It's a regular -er verb and the model for the whole -er group. Comer fora means to eat out.

quick.en: What do you want to eat?

presente.en: Do you eat meat or are you vegetarian?

presente.pt: Ao domingo, [comemos] em casa dos meus pais.
presente.en: On Sundays, we eat at my parents' house.
Portuguese people eat a lot of salt cod.

perfeito.pt: [Comi] um pastel de nata ao pequeno-almoço.
perfeito.en: I had a custard tart for breakfast.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I didn't eat vegetables.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [comia] sempre pão com tudo.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather always ate bread with everything.

imperfeito.pt: [Comíamos] sardinhas nas festas de Santo António.
imperfeito.en: We used to eat sardines at the Santo António festivities.
They were eating while they watched the game.

futuro.en: I'll eat fewer sweets this year.
Will you eat with us on Saturday?
We'll eat at eight.
The guests will eat on the terrace.

condicional.en: I'd eat another one, but I'm full.
Would you eat octopus?
He would eat everything if he could.

condicional.pt: Nós [comeríamos] fora mais vezes, mas é caro.
condicional.en: We would eat out more often, but it's expensive.

presente.en: What do you want to eat?

imperfeito.en: I didn't use to eat vegetables.
We used to eat at my grandmother's on Sundays.
imperfeito.pt: Comíamos em casa da minha avó aos domingos.

imperfeito.en: They were eating when I arrived.
imperfeito.pt: Eles estavam a comer quando cheguei.

futuro.en: Let's eat!
What are you going to eat?
We're going to eat out tonight.

condicional.en: I would eat another one.
Would you eat octopus?
We would eat outside, but it's cold.
condicional.pt: Comeríamos lá fora, mas está frio.

notes.presente: For something happening now: estou a comer. Comer fora = to eat out.
notes.perfeito: Já comeste? (Have you eaten yet?) is a very common question: EP uses the perfeito where English often uses 'have you...'. Comemos is the same in the present and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Não comia legumes = a past habit. Não comi nada ontem = a specific occasion.
notes.futuro: Vamos comer! = Let's eat! In everyday speech: o que vais comer?

patterns.en: to have a bite to eat

compare.en: to have lunch / to have dinner

recap: Em Portugal come-se muito bem! (In Portugal you eat really well!)

intro: Beber means to drink. It's a regular -er verb. For coffee, people in Portugal often say tomar (tomar um café), but beber works for any drink.

quick.en: What do you want to drink?
Shall we go for a drink?
I've already had too much to drink.

presente.pt: Eu [bebo] dois litros de água por dia.
presente.en: I drink two litres of water a day.

presente.pt: O meu pai [bebe] vinho tinto ao jantar.
presente.en: My father drinks red wine with dinner.

presente.pt: Nós [bebemos] um café depois do almoço.
presente.en: We have a coffee after lunch.

perfeito.en: Did you drink all the milk?
He drank too much at the party.
We drank vinho verde in the Minho.

imperfeito.en: I used to drink a lot of fizzy drinks.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [bebia] sempre um copo de vinho ao almoço.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather always had a glass of wine with lunch.

imperfeito.pt: [Bebíamos] chá em casa da minha avó.
imperfeito.en: We used to drink tea at my grandmother's.
They were drinking beer on the terrace.

futuro.en: This week I'll drink only water.
Will you have a drink with us?

futuro.pt: Ele não [beberá] nada, porque vai conduzir.
futuro.en: He won't drink anything because he's driving.
We'll drink to your health!

condicional.en: I would have a coffee now.
Would you have a tea?

condicional.pt: Nós [beberíamos] mais água, se nos lembrássemos.
condicional.en: We would drink more water if we remembered.
They would drink champagne if they won.

presente.en: She drinks a lot of water.

perfeito.en: We drank a bottle of wine.

imperfeito.en: I used to drink a lot of fizzy drinks.
We used to drink tea at my grandmother's.
imperfeito.pt: Bebíamos chá em casa da minha avó.

imperfeito.en: They were drinking on the terrace.
imperfeito.pt: Eles estavam a beber na esplanada.

futuro.en: Shall we go for a drink?
What are you going to drink?
I'm not going to drink tonight.

condicional.en: I would have a coffee.
Would you have some tea?
I would drink water, not wine.

notes.presente: Ordering: E para beber? (And to drink?) Uma água, por favor. For coffee, tomar is very common: tomar um café.
notes.perfeito: Bebemos is the same in the present and the perfeito; context tells you which.
notes.imperfeito: In everyday speech, the imperfeito often replaces the conditional: Bebia um café = I'd have a coffee.
notes.futuro: Vamos beber um copo? = Shall we go for a drink? (literally 'drink a glass').

patterns.en: to drink water / wine / a coffee

compare.en: to have / to take (a coffee, a pill, the bus)

recap: Vamos beber um copo para celebrar? (Shall we go for a drink to celebrate?)

en: to enjoy / to take advantage of
intro: Aproveitar means to make the most of, to enjoy or to take advantage of. It's a regular -ar verb and a very Portuguese one: Aproveita! (Enjoy it! / Make the most of it!).

quick.en: Enjoy! / Make the most of it!
I took the chance to rest.
We have to make the most of the sun.

presente.pt: Eu [aproveito] o fim de semana para descansar.
presente.en: I use the weekend to rest.
Do you make good use of your free time?
She always takes advantage of the sales.

presente.pt: Nós [aproveitamos] o bom tempo para ir à praia.
presente.en: We make the most of the good weather to go to the beach.

presente.pt: Os turistas [aproveitam] o sol do Algarve.

perfeito.pt: [Aproveitei] a viagem para visitar o Porto.
perfeito.en: I took advantage of the trip to visit Porto.
We made the most of the day.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [aproveitava] cada minuto na praia.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to enjoy every minute at the beach.

imperfeito.pt: A minha avó [aproveitava] tudo e não deitava nada fora.
imperfeito.en: My grandmother made use of everything and threw nothing away.
We used to make the most of Sundays to go out for walks.
They used to use lunchtime to chat.

futuro.en: I'll take the chance to read on the plane.
Will you take advantage of the trip to see Sintra?
We'll make the most of the bank holiday to rest.
You'll really enjoy it, I'm sure.

condicional.pt: Eu [aproveitaria] melhor o tempo, se fosse a ti.
condicional.en: I'd make better use of the time if I were you.
Would you take this opportunity?

condicional.pt: Ele [aproveitaria] mais, se não trabalhasse tanto.
condicional.en: He would enjoy it more if he didn't work so much.
We would take the chance to see the family.

presente.en: We make the most of the sun.
I'm making the most of my time in Lisbon.
presente.pt: Estou a aproveitar o meu tempo em Lisboa.

perfeito.en: I took the chance to rest.
We made the most of the day.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother never wasted anything.
We used to make the most of Sundays.
I was enjoying the sun.

futuro.en: We're going to make the most of it.
I'm going to take the chance to visit my family.
futuro.pt: Vou aproveitar para visitar a família.

futuro.en: Are you going to enjoy the beach?

condicional.en: I would make the most of it.
Would you take this opportunity?
We would use the time better.

notes.presente: Aproveitar has no single English equivalent: to enjoy, to make the most of, to use well. Aproveita! is how you wish someone a good time. Aproveitar para + infinitivo = to take the chance to.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: aproveitámos (we enjoyed) vs. aproveitamos (we enjoy).
notes.imperfeito: Aproveitar tudo also means not wasting anything (food, leftovers, materials).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vamos aproveitar, vou aproveitar para...

patterns.pt: aproveitar o dia / as férias / o sol
patterns.en: to make the most of the day / holidays / sun

recap: A vida é curta: aproveita cada momento! (Life is short: make the most of every moment!)

intro: Pagar means to pay. It's a regular -ar verb; just watch the spelling of paguei (g becomes gu before e to keep the hard sound). The past participle is pago.

presente.en: Are you paying by card or in cash?

presente.pt: O meu irmão [paga] a renda ao dia um.
presente.en: My brother pays the rent on the first of the month.
They pay a lot for the house.

perfeito.en: I paid twenty euros for dinner.
Have you paid the electricity bill yet?
We paid for the hotel before arriving.

imperfeito.en: Before, I used to pay for everything in cash.
The company used to pay very well.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [pagávamos] menos de renda em Coimbra.
imperfeito.en: We used to pay less rent in Coimbra.
Customers used to pay on the way out.

futuro.en: I'll pay the invoice tomorrow.

futuro.pt: Tu [pagarás] os cafés da próxima vez.
futuro.en: You'll pay for the coffees next time.

futuro.pt: O seguro [pagará] o arranjo do carro.
futuro.en: The insurance will pay for the car repair.
We'll pay in instalments.

condicional.pt: Eu [pagaria] mais por uma casa com varanda.
condicional.en: I would pay more for a flat with a balcony.
How much would you pay for this painting?
We would pay, but they don't take cards.

condicional.pt: Eles [pagariam] o dobro para ver este concerto.
condicional.en: They would pay double to see this concert.

imperfeito.en: I used to pay in cash.
The job paid well.
We used to pay less rent.

futuro.en: I'm going to pay tomorrow.
Who is going to pay?
You're going to pay for this!

condicional.en: I would pay more for a view.
How much would you pay?
They would pay double.

notes.presente: Pago eu! = It's on me! Pagar a meias = to split the bill. Pagar com cartão / em dinheiro = to pay by card / in cash.
notes.perfeito: Spelling: paguei keeps the hard g sound. European spelling: pagámos (we paid) vs. pagamos (we pay).
notes.imperfeito: Pagava em dinheiro = a past habit. Paguei em dinheiro = one payment.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: quem vai pagar? Vais pagar por isto! = You'll pay for this!

patterns.en: to pay by card / in cash

recap: Hoje o jantar é por minha conta: pago eu! (Dinner's on me tonight: I'm paying!)

intro: Viajar means to travel. It's a regular -ar verb. Use viajar de (comboio, avião, carro) for the means of transport, viajar para for the destination and viajar por for travelling around a place.

quick.en: We're going to travel in the summer.

presente.pt: Eu [viajo] muito por causa do trabalho.
presente.en: I travel a lot for work.
Do you travel alone or with someone?

presente.pt: Nós [viajamos] para o Algarve todos os verões.
presente.en: We travel to the Algarve every summer.

perfeito.en: I travelled around Europe last year.
Have you ever been to the Azores?
He travelled by coach to Madrid.
We travelled around the Alentejo by car.

imperfeito.en: When I was a student, I used to hitchhike.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [viajava] muito em trabalho.
imperfeito.en: My father used to travel a lot for work.
We always used to travel in August.
My grandparents used to travel by boat.

futuro.en: I will travel to Brazil in December.
Where will you travel on holiday?
We will travel by plane.

futuro.pt: Eles [viajarão] pela Ásia durante um ano.
futuro.en: They will travel around Asia for a year.

condicional.en: I would travel more if I had the money.
Would you travel alone?
He would travel all over the world.

condicional.pt: Nós [viajaríamos] de comboio, mas é muito lento.
condicional.en: We would travel by train, but it's very slow.

perfeito.en: Have you ever travelled to the Azores?

imperfeito.en: I used to travel a lot.
We always used to travel in August.
My father used to travel for work.
imperfeito.pt: O meu pai viajava em trabalho.

futuro.en: We're going to travel in the summer.
Where are you going to travel?
I'm going to travel by car.

condicional.en: I would travel more if I had time.
Would you travel alone?
We would travel around the world.

notes.presente: Viajar de + transport: de comboio, de avião, de carro (but a pé, on foot). Viajar para = to travel to; viajar por = to travel around. The noun is a viagem: Boa viagem!
notes.perfeito: European spelling: viajámos (we travelled). Já viajaste para...? = Have you ever travelled to...?
notes.imperfeito: Viajava à boleia = I used to hitchhike (à boleia is PT-PT; Brazil says de carona).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vamos viajar, para onde vais viajar?

patterns.en: to travel by train / plane / car

compare.en: to go for a walk / to stroll / to sightsee

recap: Adoro viajar de comboio pelo vale do Douro! (I love travelling by train through the Douro valley!)
